atoms.name: mod
atoms.rule: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: neg
atoms.rule: - a is the negation of a.
atoms.plain: - a is the negation of a.

atoms.name: pitch_transpose
atoms.rule: a ♯ b moves MIDI note a by b semitones; a result outside 0 through 127 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ♯ b moves MIDI note a by b semitones; a result outside 0 through 127 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_octave_up
atoms.rule: a ⇈ raises MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result above 127 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇈ raises MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result above 127 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_octave_down
atoms.rule: a ⇊ lowers MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result below 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇊ lowers MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result below 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_interval
atoms.rule: a ⟷ b is the signed number of semitones from note a to note b.
atoms.plain: a ⟷ b is the signed number of semitones from note a to note b.

atoms.name: pitch_invert
atoms.rule: a ⇅ b reflects every pitch in melody a around MIDI note b and keeps durations; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇅ b reflects every pitch in melody a around MIDI note b and keeps durations; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_retrograde
atoms.rule: a ⟲ reverses the order of melody a, keeping each note with its duration.
atoms.plain: a ⟲ reverses the order of melody a, keeping each note with its duration.

atoms.name: pitch_scale_step
atoms.rule: a ♬ is the next higher note in C major; no higher MIDI note gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ♬ is the next higher note in C major; no higher MIDI note gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_major_triad
atoms.rule: a △ builds a three note major triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 4, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a △ builds a three note major triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 4, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_minor_triad
atoms.rule: a ▽ builds a three note minor triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 3, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ▽ builds a three note minor triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 3, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_repeat
atoms.rule: a ⥁ b repeats melody a b times for b from 0 through 16; other counts give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⥁ b repeats melody a b times for b from 0 through 16; other counts give NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_concat
atoms.rule: a ⋈ b plays melody a followed by melody b.
atoms.plain: a ⋈ b plays melody a followed by melody b.

atoms.name: pitch_melody_equal
atoms.rule: a ≎ b is true when melodies a and b have the same pitches and beat durations.
atoms.plain: a ≎ b is true when melodies a and b have the same pitches and beat durations.

atoms.name: pitch_note_equal
atoms.rule: a ≐ b is true when the two MIDI notes have the same pitch.
atoms.plain: a ≐ b is true when the two MIDI notes have the same pitch.

domain.en: A note is a MIDI number from 0 to 127; 60 is C4. A melody is a list of notes with durations in beats.
Integers give semitone steps, repeat counts and recursive counts.

settings.en: The key and scale used by the scale step ♬.
A recursive call repeats its step at most this many times; larger counts give NaN.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: ●₁
operators.plain: Append b to a, then reverse its notes.

operators.name: ♤₂
operators.plain: If a equals [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2], apply ♠₄₄ to a and 4, then append [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2] to it; otherwise compute a ♠₄₄ 4.

operators.name: ☆₃
operators.definition: a ☆₃ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ☆₃ (b - 1)) ★₂₄, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ☆₃ (b + 1)) ★₂₄, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ★₂₄ to the current value.

operators.name: ◆₄
operators.plain: Append a with its notes in reverse order to [D4:1 F4:2].

operators.name: ♦₅
operators.plain: Transpose a by b semitones, then apply ◆₇ to the result.

operators.name: ♧₆
operators.plain: Mirror a around b, then reverse its notes.

operators.name: ◆₇
operators.plain: Build a major triad on a, then repeat it once.

operators.name: ♡₈
operators.plain: Move a up one step of C major, then apply ◆₇ to the result.

operators.name: ♧₉
operators.plain: Move a up one step of C major, then apply ♡₈ to the result.

operators.name: ▲₁₀
operators.plain: Build a major triad on a, then reverse its notes.

operators.name: ♣₁₁
operators.plain: Test whether [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2] equals a ♧₉.

operators.name: ☆₁₂
operators.plain: Lower a an octave, then apply ▲₁₀ to the result.

operators.name: □₁₃
operators.plain: Apply ♦₅ to a and b, then mirror it around C5.

operators.name: ♣₁₄
operators.plain: Transpose a by b semitones, then test whether the result is the same note as C3.

operators.name: ♦₁₅
operators.plain: Lower a an octave, then apply ♣₁₄ to the result and 2.

operators.name: ♡₁₆
operators.plain: Apply ♦₅ to a and b, then test whether the result equals [G4:1].

operators.name: ○₁₇
operators.plain: Transpose a by b semitones, then apply □₁₃ to the result and 4.

operators.name: ▼₁₈
operators.plain: Mirror [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2] around a an octave higher.

operators.name: ♦₁₉
operators.plain: Apply ▼₁₈ to a, then apply ♧₆ to the result and G4.

operators.name: ♧₂₀
operators.plain: Append the major triad on a to [D4:1 F4:2].

operators.name: ◆₂₁
operators.definition: a ◆₂₁ b = { (a ♦₅ b) ⟲, if a ≐ 72; a ♦₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ♦₅ to a and b, then reverse its notes; otherwise compute a ♦₅ b.

operators.name: ♡₂₂
operators.definition: a ♡₂₂ b = { (a ♯ b) ⇈, if a ≐ 48; a ♯ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C3, transpose a by b semitones, then raise it an octave; otherwise transpose a by b semitones.

operators.name: ♡₂₃
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, build a minor triad on a, then reverse its notes; otherwise build a minor triad on a.

operators.name: ★₂₄
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C3, move a up one step of C major, then apply ♡₂₂ to the result and 3; otherwise move a up one step of C major.

operators.name: ♧₂₅
operators.definition: a ♧₂₅ b = { 1 - (a ⟷ b), if a ≐ 62; a ⟷ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as D4, subtract the semitones from a to b from 1; otherwise measure the semitones from a to b.

operators.name: ♣₂₆
operators.plain: If a is the same note as E4, apply ▼₁₈ to a, then mirror it around D4; otherwise apply ▼₁₈ to a.

operators.name: ♣₂₇
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, append a ▲₁₀ to [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2]; otherwise apply ▲₁₀ to a.

operators.name: ♢₂₈
operators.definition: a ♢₂₈ b = { (a ♦₅ b) ♧₆ 60, if a ≐ 72; a ♦₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ♦₅ to a and b, then apply ♧₆ to the result and C4; otherwise compute a ♦₅ b.

operators.name: ♢₂₉
operators.plain: If a is the same note as G4, apply ◆₇ to a, then mirror it around G4; otherwise apply ◆₇ to a.

operators.name: ♦₃₀
operators.plain: If a is the same note as G4, apply ♣₂₆ to a, then repeat it 0 times; otherwise apply ♣₂₆ to a.

operators.name: ○₃₁
operators.definition: a ○₃₁ b = { [[67, 1]] ⋈ (a ♦₅ b), if a ≐ 72; a ♦₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, append a ♦₅ b to [G4:1]; otherwise compute a ♦₅ b.

operators.name: ▲₃₂
operators.definition: a ▲₃₂ b = { (a □₁₃ b) ⇅ 62, if a ≐ 64; a □₁₃ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as E4, apply □₁₃ to a and b, then mirror it around D4; otherwise compute a □₁₃ b.

operators.name: ★₃₃
operators.plain: If a is the same note as D4, build a minor triad on a, then reverse its notes; otherwise build a minor triad on a.

operators.name: ●₃₄
operators.plain: Append a ♡₈ to [D4:1 F4:2].

operators.name: ♤₃₅
operators.plain: Apply ◆₂₁ to C4 and (a ♧₂₅ b).

operators.name: ♠₃₆
operators.definition: a ♠₃₆ b = { (a ⥁ b) ⟲, if a ≎ [[67, 1]]; a ⥁ b, else }
operators.plain: If a equals [G4:1], repeat a b times, then reverse its notes; otherwise repeat a b times.

operators.name: ◆₃₇
operators.plain: Apply ♣₂₇ to a, then append [D4:1 F4:2] to it.

operators.name: ■₃₈
operators.definition: a ■₃₈ b = { (a ○₃₁ b) ⇅ 48, if a ≐ 72; a ○₃₁ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ○₃₁ to a and b, then mirror it around C3; otherwise compute a ○₃₁ b.

operators.name: ♧₃₉
operators.plain: Apply ○₃₁ to a and b, then apply ♧₆ to the result and D4.

operators.name: ☆₄₀
operators.definition: a ☆₄₀ b = { (a ♡₂₂ b) ♯ 1, if a ≐ 60; a ♡₂₂ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply ♡₂₂ to a and b, then transpose it by 1 semitone; otherwise compute a ♡₂₂ b.

operators.name: ☆₄₁
operators.definition: a ☆₄₁ b = { (a ♡₂₂ b) ⇊, if a ≐ 72; a ♡₂₂ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ♡₂₂ to a and b, then lower it an octave; otherwise compute a ♡₂₂ b.

operators.name: ♦₄₂
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ★₃₃ to a, then apply ◆₄ to the result; otherwise apply ★₃₃ to a.

operators.name: ▲₄₃
operators.definition: a ▲₄₃ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ▲₄₃ (b - 1)) ⇊, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ▲₄₃ (b + 1)) ⇊, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): lower the current value an octave.

operators.name: ♠₄₄
operators.definition: a ♠₄₄ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♠₄₄ (b - 1)) ⟲, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ♠₄₄ (b + 1)) ⟲, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): reverse the notes in the current value.

operators.name: ♡₄₅
operators.definition: a ♡₄₅ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♡₄₅ (b - 1)) ⇈, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ♡₄₅ (b + 1)) ⇈, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): raise the current value an octave.

operators.name: ♥₄₆
operators.definition: a ♥₄₆ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♥₄₆ (b - 1)) ◆₄, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ♥₄₆ (b + 1)) ◆₄, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ◆₄ to the current value.

operators.name: ♡₄₇
operators.definition: a ♡₄₇ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♡₄₇ (b - 1)) ♬, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ♡₄₇ (b + 1)) ♬, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): move the current value up one step of C major.

operators.name: ♤₄₈
operators.plain: Mirror [G4:1] around a ♡₄₇ 1.

operators.name: ♣₄₉
operators.plain: Apply ☆₃ to a and b, then apply ◆₃₇ to the result.

operators.name: ☆₅₀
operators.plain: Apply ▲₄₃ to a and b, then lower it an octave.

operators.name: ★₅₁
operators.plain: Apply ♡₄₇ to a and b, then apply ○₃₁ to the result and 3.

operators.name: ■₅₂
operators.plain: Apply ▲₄₃ to a and 1, then apply ♧₂₅ to the result and E4.

operators.name: ☆₅₃
operators.plain: Apply ▲₄₃ to a and 1, then apply ○₁₇ to the result and 3.

operators.name: ♢₅₄
operators.plain: Apply ☆₃ to a and b, then apply ◆₂₁ to the result and 3.

operators.name: ♥₅₅
operators.plain: Append a ★₅₁ 1 to [G4:1].

operators.name: ♤₅₆
operators.plain: Apply ♥₄₆ to a and 2, then reverse its notes.

operators.name: ◆₅₇
operators.plain: Apply ♠₄₄ to a and b, then apply ♧₆ to the result and C4.

operators.name: ♧₅₈
operators.plain: Apply ☆₃ to a and 3, then apply ♧₃₉ to the result and 2.

operators.name: ♢₅₉
operators.plain: Apply ★₅₁ to a and b, then append [G4:1] to it.

operators.name: ♢₆₀
operators.plain: Apply ●₁ to [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2] and (a ♥₅₅).

operators.name: ■₆₁
operators.plain: Append a ♥₅₅ to [D4:1 F4:2].

operators.name: ▼₆₂
operators.plain: Test whether G4 is the same note as a ▲₄₃ b.

operators.name: ◆₆₃
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply ♣₄₉ to a and 1, then apply ♠₃₆ to the result and 2; otherwise compute a ♣₄₉ 1.

operators.name: ★₆₄
operators.plain: If a is the same note as D4, apply ♢₅₉ to a and 4, then mirror it around E4; otherwise compute a ♢₅₉ 4.

operators.name: ●₆₅
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply ♢₅₉ to a and 3, then apply ◆₄ to the result; otherwise compute a ♢₅₉ 3.

operators.name: ▲₆₆
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply ■₅₂ to a, then take the remainder when dividing it by 4; otherwise apply ■₅₂ to a.

operators.name: ★₆₇
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, append a ♥₅₅ to [C4:1 E4:1 G4:2]; otherwise apply ♥₅₅ to a.

operators.name: ▼₆₈
operators.definition: a ▼₆₈ b = { (a ♡₄₅ b) ☆₅₀ 4, if a ≐ 60; a ♡₄₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply ♡₄₅ to a and b, then apply ☆₅₀ to the result and 4; otherwise compute a ♡₄₅ b.

operators.name: ♧₆₉
operators.definition: a ♧₆₉ b = { (a ♡₄₅ b) ⇊, if a ≐ 72; a ♡₄₅ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ♡₄₅ to a and b, then lower it an octave; otherwise compute a ♡₄₅ b.

operators.name: ▼₇₀
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C3, apply ♢₅₄ to a and 4, then apply ♠₃₆ to the result and 0; otherwise compute a ♢₅₄ 4.

operators.name: ♠₇₁
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, append a ●₆₅ to [G4:1]; otherwise apply ●₆₅ to a.

operators.name: ▼₇₂
operators.definition: a ▼₇₂ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ▼₇₂ (b - 1)) ◆₅₇ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ▼₇₂ (b + 1)) ◆₅₇ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ◆₅₇ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ♧₇₃
operators.definition: a ♧₇₃ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♧₇₃ (b - 1)) ♧₆₉ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ♧₇₃ (b + 1)) ♧₆₉ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ♧₆₉ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ▼₇₄
operators.definition: a ▼₇₄ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ▼₇₄ (b - 1)) ▼₆₈ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ▼₇₄ (b + 1)) ▼₆₈ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ▼₆₈ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ○₇₅
operators.definition: a ○₇₅ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ○₇₅ (b - 1)) ♤₅₆, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ○₇₅ (b + 1)) ♤₅₆, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ♤₅₆ to the current value.

operators.name: ♤₇₆
operators.definition: a ♤₇₆ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♤₇₆ (b - 1)) ☆₅₀ 1, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ♤₇₆ (b + 1)) ☆₅₀ 1, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ☆₅₀ to the current value and 1.

operators.name: ●₇₇
operators.definition: a ●₇₇ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ●₇₇ (b - 1)) ♤₂, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ●₇₇ (b + 1)) ♤₂, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): apply ♤₂ to the current value.

operators.name: ★₇₈
operators.plain: Apply ♧₇₃ to a and b, then apply ★₃₃ to the result.

operators.name: ♡₇₉
operators.plain: Apply ♧₇₃ to a and b, then apply ♢₂₈ to the result and 3.

operators.name: ♥₈₀
operators.plain: Apply ♧₇₃ to a and b, then apply ♧₉ to the result.

operators.name: ◇₈₁
operators.plain: Apply ▼₇₄ to a and b, then apply ◆₃₇ to the result.

operators.name: ♤₈₂
operators.plain: Append a ◇₈₁ 2 to [D4:1 F4:2].

operators.name: ♡₈₃
operators.plain: Apply ♤₈₂ to a, then reverse its notes.

operators.name: ♣₈₄
operators.plain: Apply ♧₇₃ to a and b, then apply ♢₆₀ to the result.

operators.name: ♥₈₅
operators.plain: Apply ★₇₈ to a and 3, then apply ♤₂ to the result.

operators.name: ♦₈₆
operators.plain: Apply ★₇₈ to a and b, then apply ♠₃₆ to the result and 4.

operators.name: ▼₈₇
operators.plain: Apply ♧₇₃ to a and b, then apply ♦₅ to the result and 0.

operators.name: □₈₈
operators.plain: Apply ▼₇₄ to a and 2, then apply ◇₈₁ to the result and 2.

operators.name: ☆₈₉
operators.definition: a ☆₈₉ b = { (a ◇₈₁ b) ◆₅₇ 0, if a ≐ 64; a ◇₈₁ b, else }
operators.plain: If a is the same note as E4, apply ◇₈₁ to a and b, then apply ◆₅₇ to the result and 0; otherwise compute a ◇₈₁ b.

operators.name: ♧₉₀
operators.plain: If a is the same note as E4, apply ♥₈₀ to a and 3, then apply ●₁ to the result and [G4:1]; otherwise compute a ♥₈₀ 3.

operators.name: ○₉₁
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ♥₈₅ to a, then apply ♠₃₆ to the result and 3; otherwise apply ♥₈₅ to a.

operators.name: ■₉₂
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply ♡₇₉ to a and 2, then apply ♧₆ to the result and E4; otherwise compute a ♡₇₉ 2.

operators.name: ◇₉₃
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ★₇₈ to a and 1, then reverse its notes; otherwise compute a ★₇₈ 1.

operators.name: ♤₉₄
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C4, apply ▼₇₄ to a and 1, then apply ☆₄₁ to the result and 3; otherwise compute a ▼₇₄ 1.

operators.name: ▼₉₅
operators.plain: If a is the same note as C5, apply ♤₇₆ to a and 0, then apply ♡₂₂ to the result and 1; otherwise compute a ♤₇₆ 0.
